text: Any and all let you ask a yes-or-no question about an entire sequence at once.
all returns true only when every single item is truthy — here, only if all the numbers are even.
[chuckle] any is the opposite mood — it returns true if even one item passes the test.
So any of the numbers being greater than five is enough to make it true.
[sniff] Both are smart and short-circuit — all stops at the first false, any stops at the first true.
That makes them fast even over huge sequences, since they quit as soon as the answer is settled.
[sigh] They pair perfectly with a generator expression for validation, like checking every password is long enough.
One quirk worth memorizing: on an empty sequence, all is true and any is false.
[groan] any and all replace clunky loops-with-a-flag with one line that says exactly what you mean.
